research_question: What is the effect of indirect training combined with direct pelvic floor muscle training (PFMT), compared with direct PFMT alone, on incontinence-related quality of life in women with urinary incontinence?
treatment_label: Indirect training combined with direct PFMT
outcome_description: Incontinence-related quality of life assessed by validated condition-specific questionnaires (e.g., Incontinence Quality of Life Questionnaire [I-QOL], King's Health Questionnaire [KHQ], International Consultation on Incontinence Questionnaire-Short Form [ICIQ-UI SF], or Incontinence Impact Questionnaire [IIQ-7]).
positive_direction: A positive effect size indicates greater improvement / higher quality of life favoring indirect training combined with direct PFMT over direct PFMT alone.
search_queries: urinary incontinence pelvic floor muscle training indirect core trunk trial
urinary incontinence combined pelvic floor exercise quality of life controlled trial
pelvic floor muscle training abdominal core exercise urinary incontinence randomized
inclusion_criteria: Adult women diagnosed with urinary incontinence (stress, urgency, or mixed urinary incontinence).

Intervention arm receiving indirect training (e.g., trunk, core, hip, or general exercise without PFM contraction) combined with direct PFMT, compared against a control arm receiving direct PFMT alone.
Quantitative assessment of incontinence-related quality of life using validated condition-specific instruments.
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic reviews, meta-analyses, protocols, editorials, conference abstracts, or theoretical papers).
No comparison between indirect training combined with direct PFMT and direct PFMT alone (e.g., indirect training alone vs direct PFMT, or coordinated PFMT during movement vs direct PFMT).
No quantitative outcome data reporting incontinence-related quality of life that can produce an effect size (means, standard deviations, sample sizes, or test statistics).
Completely unrelated to female urinary incontinence or exercise-based interventions.
moderators_to_extract: Type of indirect training (e.g., core stabilization, abdominal, Pilates, hip strengthening)
Type of urinary incontinence (stress, urgency, or mixed)
Intervention duration and frequency (weeks, sessions per week)
Supervision level (supervised, partially supervised, or home-based)
Specific quality of life instrument utilized (e.g., I-QOL, KHQ, ICIQ-UI SF, IIQ-7)
effect_size_note: Standardized mean differences (Hedges' g) will be calculated. Where scales measure impact/bother (higher raw score = worse), scores will be inverted so that positive effect sizes uniformly reflect superior quality of life in the combined group.
